messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate + rising p95 latency from inference-runtime.kv-layer in us-west-2. Threshold breached: 10m error rate > 3% — paging eng-oncall
Sam: acknowledging, pulling recent deploys and metrics
Priya: seeing a sharp jump in KV miss rate from 5% -> 58% around 04:06 UTC, correlates with bursty short requests. Upstream 504s spiking
Kai: any recent infra or quant changes?
Alex: I merged PR #4205 earlier (03:58) that tightened quant packing to int4-aggressive for variant-x. It touched quant profiles only
Sam: ok, immediate mitigations: 1) toggle kv cache bypass flag 2) increase batcher replicas 3) rollback quant profile if needed. Who can flip the flag?
Priya: I can flip the flag: `POST /api/flags/kv_cache/disable {env: "prod"}` — following runbook infer-kv-ops (link)
Kai: scaling batcher: `kubectl -n inference scale deploy batcher --replicas=14`
Alex: I'll prepare rollback for PR #4205 and push rollback branch -> canary
support-bot: Preparing customer notification draft for impacted tenants; will wait for mitigation confirmation
Priya: cache bypass enabled at 04:18 UTC. KV miss down to ~6%
Sam: batchers scaled, CPU normalized, latency trending down
Kai: rollback canary looks ok on 5k reqs; promoting to prod at 04:32
Alex: rollback to prod complete, monitoring
incident-bot: Alert cleared: error rate back below threshold
Sam: quick impact calc — approx 37 minutes of degraded responses, estimated 0.9% of total traffic affected. Support notified and initial customer message queued
Priya: preliminary root cause: aggressive int4 quant profile increased output variance -> more distinct KV keys + bursty short prompts exhausted batching window -> miss storm
Kai: short-term fixes: auto-bypass when KV miss > 20%, add warm standby batcher replicas, and add an emergency scale policy for burst windows
Alex: long-term: add quant profile CI checks that measure cache-key cardinality and introduce a canary traffic test exercising token variance
Sam: scheduling postmortem review — proposed: Tomorrow 15:00 UTC, 30m. Who can make it?
Kai: I can
Priya: yep
Alex: available
support-bot: Postmortem event created and ticket INF-9937 opened to track remediation, runbooks, and customer comms
Sam: action items assigned:
- Priya: implement auto-bypass trigger + alert at 15% KV miss (due EOW)
- Kai: implement prewarm and emergency scale policy for batchers; document replicas and thresholds (due 4 business days)
- Alex: add quant-profile cache-footprint tests + canary traffic harness (due 10 business days)
- Sam: draft postmortem, include timeline, mitigations, impact numbers, and follow-ups (due before review)
Priya: dropped a reproducer script into INF-9937: `tools/repro_kv_churn.sh` (parameters for token variance)
Kai: attaching scale/playbook snippets and `kubectl` commands to ticket
Alex: will open PR for CI checks and reference INF-9937
Sam: handoff: Kai will own primary monitoring until postmortem and closure of INF-9937. I'll lead the writeup
Kai: dashboard pinned in #eng-oncall, refresh interval set to 30s :mag:
Priya: one more suggestion — add a cache-key fingerprint truncation to reduce cardinality from whitespace/tokenizer noise
Sam: added to actions list
support-bot: Customer summary draft available in INF-9937; please review within 1h
Sam: thanks everyone. Closing thread — will post postmortem link once draft ready
